scenes.text: Many of today's biggest scams don't hack anyone. A fake bank officer, or a fake police call, talks the customer into sending the money themselves, so every check passes. In India, citizens lost over twenty-two thousand crore rupees to cyber crime in 2024.

Last Mile Guard is a second look before the money leaves. It checks the payment, reads the customer's own words with Gemini, and looks at the receiving account. Plain rules decide, and a person confirms every hold. The data is made up, and no money moves.

Here is one case, start to finish, on the live site. A customer is paying ninety-eight thousand five hundred rupees, while a caller who says he is from the bank is on the line. The customer app sends the payment to Last Mile Guard, and within seconds it is paused, with a notice and a reference. The customer taps Call fraud team inside the app, so it cannot be a scammer's call, and an AI agent asks two questions about this payment. On the bank's side, three checks score the payment, each with a written reason. Then Gemini acts as an investigator: it chooses its own read-only lookups, the payee, the phone's signals and the scam playbook, and cites what it used. It cannot change the score or release the payment. The analyst keeps it on hold. Only a person can release it.
The same engine reads a pasted call. This digital-arrest script, a fake police officer demanding money, is flagged high risk, with every tactic it found and the points each one adds.
To test it, Gemini plays both the scammer and the customer, with new cases it invents. The answer key stays hidden until the guard decides, and misses are shown, not hidden.

We measured it, including the bad news. On the same fifty synthetic payments, before any customer answer, payment rules alone warned or held eleven of twenty-five scams. With Gemini, thirteen. But Gemini asks instead of guessing: twenty-eight payments stopped at a question, and sixteen of twenty-five genuine customers were asked or warned. The next test is the outcome after the answer.
It runs on Google Cloud. Firebase Hosting sits in front of Cloud Run. Gemini on Vertex AI reads the words and chooses its lookups, with no keys in the code. Cases expire after twenty-four hours.
Last Mile Guard. A second look before the money moves.
